name: Screens in the Living Room: Five Golden Ages of Television
description: From live variety shows to streaming dramas, the series that kept families in front of the set and changed what television could say and show.

checkpoints.name: Television arrives
checkpoints.note: A small screen enters homes, bringing live variety, new sitcoms filmed for repeat, and the first drama anthologies. Colour television arrives in the 1950s.

checkpoints.name: Shared screens
checkpoints.note: Space adventures, satire, children's learning and the epic miniseries Roots show how many people can watch one show at once.

checkpoints.name: Ensembles and wonders
checkpoints.note: Big-cast dramas, cartoons for adults, natural-history landmarks and sitcoms about nothing reshape the schedule, and drama starts to feel like a novel. Telenovelas and Japan's Oshin win huge audiences at home and abroad.

checkpoints.name: The cable drama age
checkpoints.note: Pay channels let writers tell long, grim, complex stories, and critics begin to speak of television as the equal of film.

checkpoints.name: The streaming age
checkpoints.note: Netflix and other streaming services and global hits remove the weekly schedule, and a Spanish show and a fantasy epic find audiences in every country.
